title: Control plane connectivity regression after kernel MTU change during private upgrade
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: During a staged kernel and agent upgrade rollout to private VPC control planes, ~12% of customer clusters experienced intermittent control-plane connectivity loss. Root cause analysis points to a coordinated regression: a default MTU change applied by a kernel package combined with an iptables->nft transition on our host firewall caused conntrack-NAT entries to drop for long-running control plane connections. This primarily impacted clusters using jumbo MTU and older dataplane configs. The outage lasted up to 47 minutes for some customers before automatic rollback and manual remediation restored connectivity.
impact: Customers: 18 private clusters across 5 accounts experienced control-plane disconnects causing API timeouts, deployment rollbacks, and failed health checks. Incidents triggered support escalations and one customer reported an automated failover to backup control plane (no data loss reported). SLOs: brief SLA blips for control-plane API latency and availability for affected tenants.
detection: Oncall alerts from control-plane heartbeat failures and an aggregated spike in apiserver 5xx rates. Telemetry: sudden drop in control-plane long-lived TCP connections on nodes; correlates with upgrade window and package churn logs. Early detection delayed by masking of node-level health until control-plane endpoints fully timed out.

root_cause: Two simultaneous changes combined to create a regression. 1) A kernel package updated default MTU handling for certain network drivers, lowering effective path MTU for interfaces configured for jumbo frames; 2) the host security agent rollout replaced legacy iptables rules with nft-based chains without preserving specific conntrack/NAT exemptions for control-plane long-lived connections. The MTU shift caused fragmentation and retransmits; conntrack entries aged out because packet patterns changed and NAT table rewrites were misapplied under nft, breaking connection continuity.
mitigation: Immediate: paused rollout and rolled back kernel package for remaining cohorts; restored legacy iptables rules for affected hosts; flushed conntrack tables and restarted control-plane agent to re-establish sessions. Short-term: add a preflight check in the upgrade pipeline to validate MTU and conntrack behavior on a canary node. Long-term: add automated compatibility tests for iptables->nft transitions, ensure our firewall templates preserve conntrack exemptions, and add runtime detection to auto-flush and gracefully rebind control-plane sockets when conntrack anomalies are detected.

followup_notes: We discovered this class of regression is likely to recur when kernel or networking-related packages change default behaviors. We will prioritize cross-team gating for infra-level upgrades that can affect packetization and conntrack semantics. The mitigation checklist and automated tests should reduce blast radius for future rollouts.
